newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN-RUSSIAN BANK ADOPTS TWO-TIER MANAGEMENT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN-RUSSIAN BANK ADOPTS TWO-TIER MANAGEMENT.

text.p: The private Bulgarian-Russian Investment Bank (BRIB) said on Monday it had decided to replace its current nine-member board of directors with a two-tier management system to meet new, stricter banking requirements.
"The shareholders decided to replace the current board of directors with supervisory and execuitive boards to meet tougher requirements under the new Banking Law," a BRIB statement said.

Prior to the introduction of a currency board system on July 1 Bulgaria's parliament approved a new banking law, setting stricter requirements for bank management teams in a bid to restore confidence in local banks.
The newly elected three-member supervisory board included Contract Holding Company, BOST joint stock company and CAP Ltd as legal entities, said the statement.
The bank's executive board was expected to be appointed at a meeting of the supervisory board due to be held later, a BRIB official said.
The BRIB, which was set up in 1994, has a full banking licence for domestic and international operations. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
